description:
The committed family is single-valued today — materializers/<tag> = {worker_id, node} — which does not merely ASSUME one materializer per shard, it enforces it: any retirement predicate built on it ("the entry doesn't name me") makes a second instance for a shard suicide on startup. Bedrock intends multiple materializers per shard (settled with the user 2026-08-24): a distributor-class component seeing disproportionate traffic for a shard from one node may place an additional instance near it, or migrate one. That is a policy divergence from FDB (whose team size is fixed by the replication factor and whose DD rebalances WHICH servers rather than adding one for read locality) — but not a mechanism divergence: FDB's shard membership is already a SET (keyServers/<range> decodes to a team of server UIDs; the proxy addTags all of them), and FDB's removal notice is addressed BY KEY (serverKeys/<victim>/<range> = false), never inferred from a single value naming someone else.

SHAPE: materializers/<tag>/<worker_id> = node. Tag-major, so the routing question is a prefix scan and the per-worker fact is directly addressable. This is one family where FDB needs two (keyServers range-major for the proxy's routing, serverKeys server-major so a server can find its own ranges and be individually addressed): our notices broadcast on the shard tag rather than unicasting to a per-server tag, and a worker owns exactly one shard, so it needs no self-index. worker_id leaves the value; the value carries only the node needed to build the callable ref.

SETTLED CALLS (2026-08-24):
- PLACEHOLDER becomes an ordinary entry under the prefix (materializers/<tag>/distributor-placeholder = node) and routing prefers any real worker over it. Parking therefore stops being destructive — it ADDS rather than overwrites — which dissolves the corpse-ref window the PR #194 audit found (F5/F2: a degraded park deleted the local ref while the keyspace still named the dead worker). Healing becomes "clear the dead worker's key, ensure the placeholder": idempotent, and never destroys a live twin's entry.
- COVERAGE becomes a prefix property: covered = at least one real (non-placeholder) entry. Healing tops up rather than replacing.
- READ-PATH SELECTION: resolve_materializer(tag) starts returning a set. Minimal now — deterministic pick (first real entry by worker_id) preserving today's behavior exactly. Locality/load-aware selection is the later epic this change exists to enable; StorageRacing is its natural home.
- MIGRATION: breaking format change, no dual-shape reader. The old single-key shape cannot be read as the new one, and carrying a compat shim for a pre-release format is the speculative guard the project's convention says to delete (cf. bedrock-q67.20.7's explicit-migration stance).

BLAST RADIUS: SystemKeys (key build + parse), SystemKeys.Values (value encode/decode), SystemKeys.Reader.decode_materializer_refs (tag => ref becomes tag => set), RoutingData (materializers map + apply_mutation set/clear semantics), CommitProxy.resolve_materializer, Internal.Repo routing, the Distributor (publish_assignment, publish_placeholders, uncovered_tags, verify_assignments, heal_tag/park_tag/idle_tag, snapshot.materializer_refs), recovery's materializer_bootstrap_phase (existing_materializers_by_shard, prefer_family_named, prior_materializer_refs) and persistence_phase's diff, and olivine's rejoin_verdict.

DIVIDEND: with the victim named in the key, bedrock-q67.21.6's retirement predicate collapses to FDB's — act directly on a clear of YOUR OWN key — and the stream-replay hazard evaporates (worker ids are fresh per recruit, so a replaying instance can only encounter clears belonging to others; a resurrected worker replaying its own clear and retiring is correct).
title: materializers/<tag>/<worker_id>: membership becomes a set
